headline: Mapping risk. Understanding climate. Building resilience.
intro: I'm a disaster risk, climate resilience and geospatial researcher. I use spatial data, quantitative models and qualitative information to understand how hazards like floods, heat, cyclones and landslides affect people, cities and the infrastructure they depend on. My mission. A risk assessment only matters if it changes a decision. I try to produce analysis that planners, officials and communities can act on, and I stay close to the people and places behind the data. That is why my desk work is paired with field visits and coordination with multiple stakeholders. My long-term aim is to help make resilience a routine part of how communities, cities and infrastructure are planned, so that the people most exposed to hazards like heat, floods and storms are protected before a disaster, not after it. Where it started. I come from a mechanical engineering background, where I learned to ask how a system behaves under stress and what happens when it fails. Disasters felt like that question at a far larger scale, with one difference: here the "system" is a community, and the stress does not fall evenly. The same flood or heatwave can be a nuisance for one household and a catastrophe for another, depending on where they live, what they earn and what support they can reach. That is what pulled me towards disasters social vulnerabilities and climate risk. In 2024 I joined the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai, for an M.Sc. in Disaster Management with a specialisation in Technologies for Disaster Management, where I added geospatial and social lenses, learning that risk is a question of people and places as much as of structures. What I've built so far. At the Jamsetji Tata School of Disaster Studies, TISS Mumbai, I ranked first in my batch. My dissertation on Nagpur's urban wetlands and lakes examines how well these water bodies cool their surroundings and values their restoration for both cooling and community benefit, and it received the Best Research Project award. Alongside it, I have worked on a range of projects, field engagements and applied assignments, some collaboratively and some independently. I supported the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority with disaster planning for Kumbh Mela 2027 through Palladium Consulting India, co-facilitated a programme evaluation for RedR India, and ground-truthed green and blue spaces for a WRI India mapathon in Mumbai. Each showed me the same thing from a different side: data, institutions and communities have to meet. Where I'm heading. I am currently an M.S. Swaminathan Fellow in the Wetlands and Coastal Ecosystems (BCM) Programme Area at the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF), where I am mentored by senior scientists and work with the Foundation's regional centres and partners. The fellowship is built around research that connects science with the communities who depend on these ecosystems, and I bring a disaster management perspective to it: how floods, heat, storms and sea-level change put wetlands, coasts and the people who live by them at risk, and what evidence can help them prepare, adapt and recover. I'm always glad to talk with people working on climate resilience, disaster risk and geospatial evidence. Outside work. Away from the screen, I'm happiest travelling, cycling and trekking. Each has taught me something I use in my work: travel keeps me curious about how people live with their landscapes, cycling teaches patience and pacing over long distances, and trekking reminds me to adapt when conditions change and to rely on the people I'm walking with. They are the same habits that fieldwork asks of me, and they are a large part of how I stay resilient, adaptable and collaborative.

about_sections.x: My professional experience spans disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, programme evaluation, research and monitoring, social impact assessment, and institutional coordination. Through engagements with consulting firms, development organisations, research institutions and academic bodies, I have contributed to field-based assessments, disaster preparedness planning, stakeholder coordination, quantitative and qualitative data analysis, GIS mapping, programme evaluation and technical documentation. My work focuses on translating research and field insights into practical solutions that strengthen institutional capacities, community resilience and sustainable development.

items.t: Disaster Management Intern | Palladium Consulting India Pvt. Ltd.
items.x: Contributed to disaster risk reduction and emergency preparedness planning for Simhastha Kumbh Mela 2027 (Nashik–Trimbakeshwar), one of the world's largest mass gatherings. Supported field-level coordination and on-ground assessments to identify vulnerabilities associated with high-density gatherings, crowd management, public safety and emergency response systems. Undertook data collection, compilation and analysis to support evidence-based planning, while coordinating with government departments, local authorities and field teams. Contributed to technical documentation, reporting and the development of disaster preparedness and mitigation strategies for large-scale events.

Appointed as a Junior Evaluator for the evaluation of the India–Hosanna Saksham Vocational Training Programme (Phase 4), implemented by Hosanna Ministries. Worked alongside a Senior Evaluator and project coordinators to support the assessment of programme performance and outcomes. Contributed to survey toolkit development, field-based data collection in Ambernath, quantitative and qualitative data analysis, report preparation and stakeholder coordination. Assisted in consolidating findings and finalising the evaluation report for submission to Hosanna Ministries and RedR India.

items.t: Design Intern | Bihar State Disaster Management Authority (BSDMA)
items.x: Collaborated with senior faculty and institutional teams at the Jamsetji Tata School of Disaster Studies (JTSDS) in association with the Bihar State Disaster Management Authority (BSDMA) to support the finalisation of institutional publications and technical reports. Contributed to report design, document structuring, advanced typesetting, layout development and formatting for official publication. Worked on visual standardisation of research content, data presentation and technical documentation, ensuring consistency, readability and professional print-ready formats.

Contributed to research, monitoring and evaluation assignments through quantitative and qualitative data management, field documentation and programme monitoring. Supported transcription and translation of interviews and field data, designed and processed OMR-based survey instruments, and coordinated enumerators during data collection activities. Assisted in programme evaluation, research analysis, live project monitoring and the digitalisation of survey instruments to improve data management and monitoring workflows.

items.t: Programme Assessment Intern | Ratna Nidhi Charitable Trust
items.x: Undertook field-based programme assessment as part of the M.Sc. Disaster Management programme, focusing on educational interventions and social welfare in underprivileged communities. Conducted storybook assessments across schools to understand the utilisation and effectiveness of educational resources provided by the organisation. Supported programme implementation, field documentation, stakeholder engagement with school administrators and educators, and the collection of qualitative insights to assess programme reach and outcomes.

items.t: Climate Resilience Intern (GIS & Mapping) | World Resources Institute India
items.x: Completed a short-term internship under Abhijit Ekbote, Independent Consultant through the WRI India initiative, "A Mapathon for a Climate-Resilient Mumbai". Conducted GIS-based mapping and spatial documentation of vacant open spaces in Ward R South, Mumbai, supporting the identification of potential spaces for climate-resilient and nature-based urban interventions. Contributed to field-based data collection, structured interviews, spatial analysis and visualisation, developing practical insights into urban planning, green infrastructure and climate resilience.
